items.title: "Ninety Nine" feat. Jul
items.description:
Jul is a Vancouver native born partly out of Origins Parkour. He's a brilliant visual artist as well as a free spirit who is known for doing moves that don't have a name and interpreting spots in a completely unique way. Lots of his movement is based in improvisation and feeling, but with a deeply skilled technical background.

One of the standout features of this video is the spot selection, what on earth is that jet?? We are honored to have Jul trust our platform with his art -- it is always a happy day in the parkour community when Jul decides to release something.

items.title: 11 Years Deep
items.description: This is the video I’ve always dreamed of making. I grew up watching Storror, Team Farang, Rilla Hops and other insane athletes, wishing I could do what they did, but it never felt possible. About 10 years ago my coach said I’d get there in 5 years—I didn’t believe it, but over time I proved myself wrong, learning skills I once thought were impossible and pushing past fear. Around 7–8 years in I realized I’d become the athlete I always wanted to be, so all that was left was making a video I’d truly be proud of. I spent over 3 years filming, not rushing anything and only keeping clips that felt right, and now I can look back and think “damn, I actually did that.” This project means a lot to me—it pushed me, inspired me, and reminded me there’s always a next level. It was hard holding onto clips for so long, but it was worth it.

items.title: Charmed
items.description:
Logan Frady, this chillest man on Earth. Logan is a great friend of The Commons, and probably wants to be your friend too! Logan stands for American parkour, he puts on for his city, and put out one of the best damn projects of the year. Originally released as a paid project on thecommons.boston, it's time for Charmed to have a second release here for anybody who missed it the first time around!

Logan's style is really interesting, he's somewhat tricking-dominant in skillset but with an obvious skate and oldschool parkour influence. Logan is no slouch in trad PK as well and the resulting style is kindof "tricking in horrifying places that take top tier parkour tech".

A highlight, for example, is Logan's wall double full off of a vertical rail. Gnarly.

items.title: City Surfers
items.description: City Surfers is a documentary which was completed in 2007 as a colaboration between Street Movement and Kasper Astrup Schröder. The movie was the first of its kind in Denmark, and it won first prize for Best Danish Documentary at DAFF [Danish Adventure Film Festival] in 2007. City Surfers follow the 4 founders of Street Movement in the summer of 2007, as they train in spots aroun Copenhagen, at the Gerlev Parkour Park at Gerlev Sports Academy and finally in Paris with the founders of Yamakasi, who also play an important part in the movie. The documentary tells about a moment in the history of the Street Movement founders and should be viewed as an artistic look into the past.

items.description: At the end of 2022, the Wizzy Gang ventures to Southeast Asia to shoot a Parkour and adventure film across Vietnam, Cambodia and Thailand. Join the adventure of 9 buddies who travel halfway around the world for several months to pursue their childhood dream. The Wizzy Gang is a French parkour and cliff diving team known for their Youtube videos. On this journey, the group will encounter a multitude of problems that stand in the way of their way of life. Follow them through 3 different civilizations that have built our society and forced this group to see the world differently. With this film, they want to show a new facet of their adventures; through civilizations where the Wizzy way of life is essential: using one's environment to live life to the full.

Once again, we pushed our limits, stepped out of our comfort zone, and refused to be like everybody else — because we don’t have to, and neither do you. Just be.

items.title: Holi Shit
items.description:
Holi Shit takes a team of freerunners, geared up with a bunch of “toys” which were as great to play with as they are to watch in slow motion and follows their adventures through the abandoned suburbs of Berlin. 

During their three days journey, the freerunners and camera crew got lost more than once on the endless highways outside of Berlin Brandenburg. We also realized that the most interesting abandoned places are not only well concealed, but are well guarded by security and police. Ignoring those signs of warning the next days were packed with thrilling moments of spectacular runs and tricks but also, getting chased by ghost hunters at midnight, and getting arrested by the police while shooting a drone shot with smoke grenades on top of the tallest building in the area. Obviously not a good idea! 

Every big city has one thing in common. After a while it is quite hard to get out of a place filled with so much energy. Chasing those abandoned buildings and feeling the calmness of a place once filled with so much life was truly inspirational.

items.title: Hommage au Parkour

items.title: SCRAP
items.description: Scrap was born from the pursuit of perfection, a distant goal that harbored dissatisfaction, and disappointment. Scrap is remembering to enjoy making the moves. Scrap is putting in the moves that you might not normally do. Scrap is finishing the line even though you tapped the foot. Scrap is being happy you sent the jump, even if you didn’t stick the pre. Scrap is the practice of not restarting every stutter step.

items.title: Silver Lining
items.description: This video means more to me than I can put into words or through jumps. I fractured my ankle right when I started filming. Even when the ankle was healed pain in that bone came back and I had to have a belly surgery, caused by nothing more than the reality of having a woman body. But I wanted, maybe needed, to finish it so I kept going. It’s about finding light exactly where everything looks darkest. It’s about holding onto the silver lining.

And I know these clips have been posted on instagram but at the time I had to keep up the grind to get me out of the shithole that some people call germany. items.title: Textured Movement
items.description:
An audio-visual exploration of movement on 16mm, shot on the bolex. 

Straying away from the traditional style of capturing movement, this film approaches documenting parkour through static and closer up shots. Traditionally, parkour films are supplemented by intense, up-beat music, but I wanted to flip that idea on its head.

items.title: The Capital of Parkour
items.description:
The documentary "The Capital of Parkour" dives into the heart of Siberia to uncover the story of a unique community that thrived against all odds. Far from Russia's center, a powerful movement was born. Through triumphs and setbacks, parkour in Siberia evolved from a street sport into a life philosophy, uniting people across generations.

Journey with us to the key cities of Siberian parkour: Krasnoyarsk, Novosibirsk, and Tomsk. Each city boasts its own unique atmosphere and approach to movement, showcased through action sequences in both stark urban landscapes and natural environments.

items.title: The Mighty Botang

I went all in on this project, even putting my own training aside, and while it was a struggle at times, it became the biggest video I’ve ever made. I worked on it in secret through 2023, but in 2024 the crew joined in, training hard and saving clips just for this, which made it really special. Big thanks to Mitch for helping lead the project—this is just something for Brisbane to look back on and be proud of.

items.title: Trials Morales
items.description: Barriers in our path... Immense constructs meant to keep us enslaved, not only in body, but also in mind. Systematic structures designed to make us feel as though we will never escape them. Many have tried to climb these walls built to trap us, and many have fallen... Through this adversity, our people have grown strong and wise, and many of our people have ascended to heights once unimaginable. Even after so much progress, we have still witnessed our heroes fall... Taken from us, almost as if to tell us that we are meant to stay down... Yet here, despite the tragedies we've suffered, heroes still rise to the occasion... and they're reaching for greater heights than have ever been accomplished before. This is the story of ascendance, rising from the ashes to direct flight, out of the mud and into the sunlight... This is the story of TRIALS MORALES!

items.title: Why don’t more Girls like jumping off walls?
